A.question: Can you tell me about a time you worked on a group project, event, or team task where someone wasn't doing their share of the work? How did you handle that situation?
A.answer:
In a group project, one member kept missing meetings and hadn't started his part.

• I messaged him privately to ask if he was okay.
• He was busy with exams, so we gave him a smaller section.
• We made a shared checklist so everyone could see progress.

We finished on time. Talking calmly and privately worked better than blaming him.

A.question: Describe a time when you had multiple assignments, tasks, or deadlines piling up at the same time. How did you prioritize what to do first?
A.answer:
Last semester I had two assignments and a club event in the same week.

• I listed every task with its deadline and how long it would take.
• I did the most urgent and important work first.
• I broke big tasks into small steps so they felt manageable.
• I asked a friend to help with the event posters.

Everything got done on time. A simple list and asking for help early saved me a lot of stress.

A.question: In your opinion, what are the biggest advantages and disadvantages of using Artificial Intelligence tools (like ChatGPT) in schools and college education?
A.answer:
AI tools like ChatGPT help students, but they have risks.

Advantages:
• They explain hard topics simply.
• They help with ideas and grammar.

Disadvantages:
• Students may copy instead of learning.
• They can give wrong information.

AI works best as a study helper, not a replacement for thinking.

A.question: If someone asked you to explain how cloud storage (like Google Drive or iCloud) works compared to saving files on a USB pen drive, how would you explain it in simple words?
A.answer:
A pen drive is like keeping your files in a small box in your pocket. They are stored inside the drive, so if you lose it, the files are gone.

Cloud storage like Google Drive is like a locker in a big, secure building run by a company. Your files travel over the internet to their computers.

• You can open them on any device with internet.
• The company keeps backups, but you trust them with your data.

B.question: Tell me about a situation where something you planned (like a trip, an event, or a project) went completely wrong. How did you adapt and deal with it?
B.answer:
Last year my friends and I planned a weekend trip, and on the morning we left, our train was cancelled because of heavy rain.

• We stayed calm and looked for other options.
• We found a bus a few hours later and booked seats right away.
• I called the guesthouse so they would keep our rooms.

The trip was shorter but still fun. It taught me to always have a backup plan and focus on solutions.

B.question: Describe an instance where you had to learn a completely new skill, hobby, or subject from scratch. What was your strategy for getting good at it?
B.answer:
A couple of years ago I started learning the guitar with no musical background.

• I began with free YouTube lessons and four basic chords.
• I practised twenty minutes every day.
• I picked songs I liked, which kept me motivated.
• A friend who plays corrected my mistakes.

After a few months I could play several songs. My strategy is to start small, practise daily and get feedback.

B.question: What do you think are the positive and negative impacts of social media algorithms on how people discover news and spend their daily time?
B.answer:
Social media algorithms show us content based on what we click.

Positive:
• We quickly find topics we care about.
• Small creators can reach big audiences.

Negative:
• We mostly see views we already agree with.
• Endless feeds keep us scrolling too long.

The key is balance and a mix of sources.

B.question: Electric vehicles (EVs) are becoming very popular. What do you see as the main benefits and the main challenges or drawbacks of switching from petrol cars to electric cars?
B.answer:
EVs have clear benefits, but also challenges.

Benefits:
• No exhaust, so cleaner city air.
• Charging is much cheaper than petrol.

Challenges:
• They cost more to buy.
• Few charging stations outside cities.
• Charging takes longer than refuelling.

EVs are the future once charging gets easier and prices fall.
